_about: Reviewed evaluation cases for the NVCT corpus. Each case records a question,
whether the filings should support an answer, and - where it is unambiguous -
the filing section the evidence ought to come from.
'known_gap' marks a case the pipeline gets wrong for a reason we understand,
with 'gap_class' naming the reason. These are targets, not noise: they are
expected to be closed by the model reading the evidence (Week 5), not by
tuning retrieval thresholds until these questions happen to pass.
subject_mismatch - the evidence is about a different company, person, or
kind of thing than the question asks about.
fact_not_stated  - the evidence is on-topic but does not state the specific
figure, date, or event asked for.
Both classes share a shape: retrieval finds text that genuinely matches the
question's words. No distance floor or coverage bar separates them, because
the mismatch is in meaning, not vocabulary.

'portable' marks a case whose expectation holds for any US filer, so it can be scored against a different company with `python evaluate.py --ticker AAPL`. Cases naming this company's drug, and 'How many patents does Apple hold?' (a fair question when the loaded company is Apple), are deliberately not portable.

'question_class: exact_identifier' marks questions that name a filing section or form rather than describing a topic. They are the case the lexical half of hybrid retrieval was kept for, and were added after a proposed change scored better on every other case while silently breaking this one.

'known_gap_without_generation' marks a case retrieval alone gets wrong but a model reading the evidence gets right. It is a failure in extractive mode and a pass in generation mode, so the suite expects different things depending on which is configured - that difference is the measurement.

corpus.note: Two most recent filings per form, ingested 2026-09-03; 637 chunks.

cases.question: How much cash does the company have on hand?
cases.why: Liquidity is disclosed in MD&A and on the balance sheet.
cases.lexical_alone: abstains - the filing says 'funds', not 'cash on hand'

cases.question: What could go wrong with the business?
cases.why: Plain-English paraphrase of Item 1A.
cases.lexical_alone: returns MD&A - matches the word 'business' instead

cases.question: Who are the executive officers and what are they paid?
cases.why: Compensation tables appear in both the 10-K and the proxy.

cases.question: Has the company ever made a profit?
cases.why: Accumulated deficit and operating losses are disclosed.
cases.lexical_alone: abstains - 'profit' does not appear as such

cases.question: Describe the drug pipeline and clinical trials
cases.why: Core business description for a clinical-stage pharma company.

cases.question: Are there any pending lawsuits?
cases.why: Legal proceedings are disclosed, including when the answer is 'none'.

cases.question: What stock exchange is the company listed on?
cases.why: Disclosed on the cover page and in Item 5.
cases.section_gap_reason: Item 5 holds the literal sentence ('Our common stock is listed on the NASDAQ Capital Market'), but it lands at fusion rank 4-5: lexical rank 7, vector rank 13 at distance 0.593. Beneficial-ownership sections in the 10-K and proxy share the words 'stock' and 'listed' and outrank it. Neither a wider vector pool, a different BM25 length-normalization constant, nor per-section diversity moved it into the top 3 - all three were swept against this file and changed nothing. The answer is still supported and cited; only the section is wrong.

cases.question: Who audits the financial statements?
cases.why: The auditor's report names the firm.

cases.question: Who serves on the board of directors?
cases.why: Director biographies are a required proxy disclosure.

cases.question: Were there any related party transactions?
cases.why: Item 404 disclosure, carried in the proxy.

cases.question: What is the company voting on at the annual meeting?
cases.why: The proxy exists to describe the proposals.

cases.question: What is the CEO annual salary?
cases.why: Summary Compensation Table states base salary by year.

cases.question: Did the company sell shares under an at-the-market program?
cases.why: The ATM program is described in the 10-K, the 10-Q, and an 8-K.

cases.question: What is the price of Bitcoin?
cases.why: Wholly outside the filings; no term overlap at all.

cases.question: What was the weather in New York yesterday?
cases.why: Off-topic, but shares tokens ('New York') with the address block.

cases.question: What is the companys carbon emissions target?
cases.why: Plausible-sounding disclosure this company does not make.

cases.question: What is the target price set by analysts?
cases.why: Analyst estimates are not a filing disclosure.

cases.question: What is the CEO favourite restaurant?
cases.why: Not the kind of fact a filing contains.

cases.question: What is the companys diversity hiring target?
cases.why: This company sets no such target in these filings.

cases.question: How many patents does Apple hold?
cases.why: About a different company.
cases.gap_reason: The filings do discuss patents, so retrieval finds real, on-topic-looking evidence. Nothing at the retrieval layer knows 'Apple' is not this registrant.
cases.gap_reason_resolved: Closed by generation (subject_mismatch). Retrieval still hands over the same topically-plausible evidence - it cannot do otherwise - but the model reads it and reports that it is about a different subject, or does not state the fact asked for. Verified with gemini-3.6-flash on 2026-09-06.

cases.question: What is the CEO home address?
cases.why: Not disclosed; only the corporate address is.
cases.gap_reason: An address is present in the filing, so retrieval cannot distinguish 'an address' from 'the CEO's home address'.
cases.gap_reason_resolved: Closed by generation (subject_mismatch). Retrieval still hands over the same topically-plausible evidence - it cannot do otherwise - but the model reads it and reports that it is about a different subject, or does not state the fact asked for. Verified with gemini-3.6-flash on 2026-09-06.

cases.question: When will the FDA approve NXP900?
cases.why: No approval date exists or is disclosed; the drug is in trials.
cases.gap_reason: Risk Factors discuss FDA approval at length without stating any date. Retrieval sees a dense topical match and cannot tell that the specific fact is absent.
cases.gap_reason_resolved: Closed by generation (fact_not_stated). Retrieval still hands over the same topically-plausible evidence - it cannot do otherwise - but the model reads it and reports that it is about a different subject, or does not state the fact asked for. Verified with gemini-3.6-flash on 2026-09-06.

cases.question: How much did the company spend on advertising?
cases.why: Advertising is not a broken-out expense line for this filer.
cases.gap_reason: MD&A discusses expenses in detail, so retrieval matches on 'spend' and 'company' without any advertising figure being present.

cases.question: What did the CEO say on the earnings call?
cases.why: An earnings call transcript is not an SEC filing.
cases.gap_reason: The CEO is named throughout the proxy, so retrieval matches the person without any call transcript existing in the corpus.

cases.question: How many employees were laid off last month?
cases.why: No layoffs are disclosed, and 'last month' is not a filing period.
cases.gap_reason: Headcount and personnel costs appear in MD&A, which is topically close enough for retrieval to accept.

cases.question: What is the weather forecast for New Jersey?
cases.why: Absurd for a filing, but the company is headquartered in New Jersey.
cases.gap_reason: The state name appears in the address block and MD&A prose. That a question this obviously unanswerable still gets through is the clearest single argument for a reading step.
cases.gap_reason_resolved: Closed by the lexical distance veto. The failure was never the vector half - it placed this text at 0.78+, well past the floor. The lexical gate let it through because 'forecast' is financial vocabulary and the state name sits in the address block, and the two gates were OR'd so the weaker one decided.

cases.question: What does Item 1A disclose?
cases.why: Names a filing section directly. The lexical half exists for exactly this - an item reference is an identifier, not a meaning embeddings capture well.

cases.question: What was reported on Form 8-K?
cases.why: Names a form rather than a topic.

cases.question: What is disclosed in Item 7 of the annual report?
cases.why: Item number plus form name, no topical content at all.

cases.question: What does Item 3 say about legal proceedings?
cases.why: Item reference paired with a topic - the mixed case.
